back: Within 15 days from the date the agency contract is executed or the first application is submitted. The director verifies eligibility within 30 days.

front: Can a producer bind coverage without an appointment?
back: No. A producer may not bind coverage for an insurer unless that insurer has appointed the producer.

Within 30 days after the effective date of termination, whether or not for cause. A copy goes to the producer within 15 days (certified mail or overnight if for cause). The producer may file comments within 30 days.
Malfeasance; breach of fiduciary duty; violation of the Code; failure to perform the contract; fewer than 25 home and auto applications in 12 months. Geographic location is NOT an allowed basis.
No more than 15% of total premium placed in any 12-month period may be on the agent's own risks or those of employees, employer or business associates.

Sell: exchange a contract for money on behalf of an insurer. Solicit: attempt to sell, or urge a person to apply for a particular kind of insurance from a particular company. Negotiate: confer or advise directly about a particular contract's substantive terms.
A producer NOT appointed by the insurer with which the policy is placed. Treated as representing the insured, not the insurer.
Age 18+; no 1239(1) act; prelicensing education completed; fees paid; exam passed for each line.
40 hours for the combined property and casualty producer/solicitor program (also covers personal lines); 20 for property only, casualty only, or personal lines only. Must include ethics instruction.
Needs its own producer license and must designate an individual licensed producer responsible for its compliance with Michigan insurance laws.
Apply for a resident license within 90 days after establishing legal residence. No prelicensing education or exam for lines already held.
Up to 180 days, no exam. For example, a surviving spouse or personal representative of a deceased or disabled producer, or the designee of a producer entering military service.

A natural person who solicits applications and collects premiums for a licensed resident agent, under a written contract, with the agent having notified the director. An agent must immediately notify the director when a solicitor's authority ends.
Signed by counselor and client BEFORE services. States the work and the fee. The fee may NOT be waived. Discloses any commission. Kept at least 2 years.

front: Who needs no counselor license to advise?
back: A licensed agent giving customary advice, and an attorney admitted in Michigan.
Prohibited for anyone required to be licensed. Renewal or deferred commissions are OK if the person was licensed at the time of sale. May be paid to an agency.
Notify the commissioner within 30 days (legal name or address; also mailing and email address).
Notify the commissioner BEFORE using any name other than the legal name.
Administrative action: within 30 days after final disposition. Criminal prosecution: within 30 days after the initial pretrial hearing date.
24 hours every 2 years, with at least 3 in ethics. Hour = at least 50 minutes. Carryover: up to 12 hours, but ethics hours don't count toward the next period's ethics requirement.
No new sales or binding; may service existing policies and receive commissions on them. License canceled if CE is still unmet after 90 days.
May reinstate without an exam within 12 months of the lapse.
Any felony within 10 years before application; regardless of date, felonies involving violence, criminal sexual conduct, or fiduciary or financial crimes (fraud, embezzlement, bribery, extortion).
Up to $1,000 per violation, or $5,000 if the person knew or should have known; max $50,000 per order. Knowingly violating a cease and desist order: up to $20,000 per violation, max $100,000.
$1,000 per violation, $10,000 aggregate; knowing violations $5,000 each, $50,000 aggregate per 6 months. Violating a cease and desist order: up to $20,000 per violation (2040).
A knowingly misleading representation or incomplete comparison of policies to induce a lapse, surrender or replacement.
License revoked, with no new license for 1 year; misdemeanor fine up to $100 per violation. An insured who accepts a rebate has coverage reduced proportionally plus a fine of up to $100.
Merchandise costing the insurer $50 or less per calendar year.
Agreeing to or concertedly committing acts that unreasonably restrain the business of insurance is an unfair trade practice.

A false, or maliciously critical or derogatory, statement about the financial condition of a person engaged in the business of insurance (an insurer, agent or agency), calculated to injure that person.

Premiums must be segregated, not commingled. Own money only to open the account and pay bank charges. Federally insured institution; may earn interest. Late remittance = prima facie fiduciary violation.
Felony: up to 4 years and/or $50,000, plus restitution. Conspiracy: up to 10 years and/or $50,000.
A person paid by a practitioner to procure clients or patients to obtain insurance benefits or assert claims. Using or acting as one with intent to defraud is a fraudulent insurance act.

Initial notice no later than when the customer relationship is established; annual notice at least once in any 12 consecutive months; a 30-day opt-out window after mailing is reasonable. Never solely oral.

Under the Insurance Data Security chapter (eff. Jan. 20, 2021), a licensee must keep a comprehensive WRITTEN information security program with administrative, technical and physical safeguards. Licensees with fewer than 25 employees, including independent contractors, are exempt from that program requirement. A qualifying cybersecurity event must be reported to the director within 10 business days. Violating chapter 5 (privacy) or its rules is an unfair trade practice.
